$comment: The Agent Skills specification frontmatter, vendored from https://agentskills.io/specification (retrieved 2026-09-22). The specification publishes no version identifier, so the _v1 suffix is ours and a future revision should land as a visible diff here. Only specification rules belong in this file: GitLab's own limits live in Skills::Validator. One specification rule is absent because draft-07 cannot express it: `name` must equal the parent directory name, which compares the instance against its file path. Skills::Validator checks that in Ruby.

name.description: Skill name. Lowercase alphanumerics and single hyphens, no leading or trailing hyphen. Must also equal the parent directory name.

description.description: What the skill does and when to use it. Loaded at agent startup alongside the name, so it is the text a runtime matches against.

license.description: License name, or a reference to a license file bundled in the skill directory.

compatibility.description: Environment requirements, such as the intended product or required system packages. Most skills omit this.

metadata.description: Free-form string map for properties the specification does not define.

allowed-tools.description: Space-separated list of tools the skill may run without further approval. Experimental in the specification; support varies between agents.

$comment-additional-properties: Unknown top-level keys are permitted even though the specification designates `metadata` as its extension point. A skill authored for another agent may carry keys we do not know about, and rejecting the whole file for one unrecognised key would make a catalog item go stale for no benefit to the reader.
